utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: We obtained the information that a military vehicle had hit a mine or there had been a detonation that had damaged the vehicle and there had been casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you also obtain information to the effect that when the Macedonian forces sought to rescue the injured, the NLA or EAAG, as you would call them, fired upon the rescuers; is that information you had in your possession?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I will at this stage ask that the investigator's note be marked for identification. We don't intend to tender those at this stage, but simply for facilitation purposes, I think I will come back to them and it would be easier to refer to a number, perhaps than to the complete ERN.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So you're looking at tab 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Tab 1, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And that will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Please, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 1D12, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can I ask the assistance of the registry, I'd like to show Rule 65 ter 230; ERN number N001-5304, N001-5306.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Bolton, that's in your binder at tab number 3. Sir, would you agree that this appears to be a so-called spot report in relation to the 10th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I would agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And could you explain, perhaps very briefly, what spot reports stand for in the OSCE language?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: It is to differentiate between routine reports. The field operations of the OSCE have a reporting responsibility to the Secretariat, and this may, depending on the field operation, be on a daily basis or a weekly basis normally. The more to report, the more regular these regular reports would be. A spot report would be a specific report relating to a specific event that was of relevance to the operations of the -- of the field operation concerned, so it would be in addition to the regular reporting process.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can I ask you perhaps to focus on the second page of this document under the subheading "central Area," and it says as follows: "At and 840 hours, an army truck struck a mine which had apparently been placed in the early hours of the morning." Would you agree that this is the event that we have been talking about?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: It would certainly appear to be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if I go on to the next paragraph, it says this: "There ensued an exchange of fire, and helicopters carried out missions in the area while wounded and dead were recovered." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it goes on to say this: "From the time of the incident, and throughout the day, the village of Ljuboten was the focal point by for operation by security forces, using mortar and small arms." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I can see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And would you agree that this is generally consistent with your own observation of that day?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Generally, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we will offer this document at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 1D13, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you a few question, sir, if you can recall about the reaction to these events that you have been giving evidence about. Would you recall that this particular evidence was condemned by the Macedonian government as a terrorist attack? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I don't recall that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, I will ask the registry to bring up what is now marked as P45.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That is, again, the white book, sir, or an excerpt thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the exact page would be N005-7606, and it is under -- 07, I'm sorry. I'm being corrected. So that would be N005-7606 to 00 -- no, 0067. We'll manage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, again, that is an excerpt of the book which you were shown by the Prosecution earlier on. Can you see that? And this is, sir, a letter from the prime minister of Macedonia, Mr. Gorgevski, to the Secretary-General of the United Nations, Mr. Kofi Annan. It's under tab number 5. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if I may draw your attention to the last paragraph but one, on this page, there is a sentence which reads as follows: "The latest terrorist attacks by the Albanian paramilitary army, in which 20 Macedonian soldiers were massacred." Can you find that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is the last paragraph but one. It starts with the word, "I will remind you once again."

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And as you will see, there is a sentence which reads: "The latest terrorist attacks by Albanian paramilitary army, in which 20 Macedonian solders were massacred." Sir, from the content of that document, would you agree that this refers or this appears to refer to both attacks, in relation to which you have given evidence it?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Would appear to do so, yes. The numbers add up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We'll also tender this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's P45. So we understand that the entire document has been received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Then why do you want this separately?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We don't need it separately, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may then proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, that this attack or attacks were also condemned by members of the international community?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I do believe that they were, yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall these attacks being condemned by a representative of the United States of America, sir?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I do not recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please assist by bring up document 1D-114. It is 1D00-1887.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, sir, that is a document which is under tab 6 of your binder. So this is a press article from the AP company, and it is dated the 10th of August, 2001. "It reports an incident," it starts in those, "At least eight Macedonian soldiers and six were killed and six were injured after a truck hit a land-mine, Friday, close to Skopje, threatening a tentative peace deal to avert all out war in Macedonia." The Defence Ministry said that. Can you say that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I can see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it is -- in the third paragraph, it says: "The explosion occurred some ten, six miles north of the capital, near the village of Ljubanci and Ljuboten, when a convoy of only trucks drove over a land-mine that had been planted." A defence military official told the Associated Press. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The court reporter asks to slow down. It is in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We will slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, may I your attention to a particular paragraph further down in this statement, which starts with the word, "No one supports." Can you say that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you will see from the previous paragraph that those words which I read to you are attributed to Mr. James Pardue. Can you tell this Chamber who Mr. Pardue is and was at the time?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Hi no dealings with Mr. Pardue, but I seem to recall that he was the US representative in the negotiations that were ongoing at the time. He was the representative of the US dealing with this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what Mr. Pardue had to say about this incident is as follows: "No one supports the Albanian extremists, certainly not the United States nor any of our European allies. The use of force by the Albanian extremists in Macedonia is unacceptable and totally rejected by the United States." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will seek to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D14, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, can you recall at that time that the incident that you record was also strongly condemned by the Security Council of the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: No, I can't. At the time, I was dealing with many issues on the ground, and that was above my pay level.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to show you a document then, if that may assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is 1D-115 and its ERN is 1D00-2009, and it's under tab 7 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: As you will see from this document, sir, it is a statement which is attributed to the president of the Security Council of the United Nations, and it is dated 13th of August, 2001. If you look at the second paragraph of that document, it welcomes the signing of the framework agreement, thereby indicating that it was adopted later on the 13th. It goes on to say this in the fourth paragraph. It reiterates -- the Security Council reiterates: It is called to all who have contact with extremist groups to make clear to them that they have no support from any quarter in the international community." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "The Council condemns the ongoing violence by extremists and calls on all parties to respect the cease-fire. The Council rejects any attempt to use violence, including the use of the land-mines to undermine the framework agreement which has been negotiated by the democratically elected political leadership of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We tender that document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D15, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, you have explained earlier today the reasons why you were using the expression EAAG when referring to the NLA. Is that correct that you were also attempting to avoid using the term "terrorist," which was perhaps loaded?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yeah. The word"terrorist" in that environment at that time was defined by different people in different ways; and to avoid that confusion, again, the purpose of usage of the expression "ethnic Albanian armed group" was to avoid confusion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You would agree that the term "terrorist" was used regularly to describe the NLA?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Not regularly by the international community.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But would you agree that it was sometimes used even by the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: It may have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If may assist, I'll ask the court -- the Registry to bring up document 1D-119 under the ERN 1D00-1587.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, sir, that is under the tab 11 of your court binder. As you can see, it's the record of the Parliamentary Assembly resolution adopted by the Parliamentary Assembly of the OSCE in Paris on the 6th and 10th of July, 2001. Can you recall that event?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll ask the Registry to assist by moving to the fourth page of that document. That would be 1D00-1590.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, sir, I will ask you to focus on paragraph 32 of the Assembly's resolution on South-east Europe? Paragraph 32 reads as follows: "Believes conflict in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia and southern Serbia has the potential to destabilise the entire region." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it goes on to say this at paragraph 33: "Apposes ethnic Albanian groups in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, Kosovo, and southern Serbia, who have instigated violence this past year. Condemns repeated acts of terrorism in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And at paragraph 34, it reiterates its full attachment to the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So what the assembly of parties of the OSCE was saying, in essence, was that they regarded this attack as terrorist attacks; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm not in a position to say that they linked the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, what the text says that they condemned "repeated acts of terrorism," and you will understand that to refer to the incidents such as the laying the land-mines or other similar activities; wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, the witness has said he is unable to link what is in this paragraph to acts of terrorism and what he saw in Macedonia. I am wondering what we would accomplish by going further with this?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I can clarify this, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You can proceed, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, so that is clear, my question may have been badly phrased, but I'm not suggesting that this would refer specifically to the incident that you witnessed. But would it be fair to suggest that this expression "repeated acts of terrorism" would or could refer to incidents such as the one that you have personally witnessed it?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: It could and I believe does refer to incidents of a nature not defined in this paragraph that occurred in Macedonia, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. And, sir, just for our information, at that stage, how many state parties were members of the OSCE, if you can recall, approximately?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: At that time, I believe it was 55 participating states of the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. So this would, essentially, be the view, I mean the common view, of those 55 states. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Of the Parliamentary Assembly of the those 55 state, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. And I think you have referred earlier to your experience or your knowledge of the conflict in Northern Ireland. Can you remember that? Not your personal experience, but your knowledge of activities in Northern Ireland. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what you understood, sir, from this knowledge -- well, I mean, let me rephrase that. You understood that at that time the IRA, Irish Republican Army, was using similar devices; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Could you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, was that -- the point of your comment earlier about your familiarity was it to underline the fact that the IRA was also using explosive of this sort that you saw under the road?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I was referring to the tactic of using explosives in -- in drainage tunnels, culverts under roads as a means of attacking the security forces, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is that correct, sir, that the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, was commonly regarded as a terrorist group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, but not because of the use of that tactic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you have indicated, also, that you were a member of the British Army for 11 years, I believe, and I hope you will be able to confirm that the British government and the British Army never regarded what are refer to as the troubles, I think, as an armed convict; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: It was referred to as "The Conflict" in Northern Ireland.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But the government never regarded the situation as being an armed conflict; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I believe that is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that in your activity, yours or of that your colleague, you had the opportunity to record a number of crimes committed by the NLA?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters comment: Could Mr. Mettraux speak slower, please. The interpreters are not able to follow thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understood the question. I recorded incidents and events, and attended the scenes of number of those events, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is that correct that some other colleagues of yours recorded similar events of crimes being committed by the members of the NLA during this crisis period?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Again, they had the same role as I did. Many people in the organisation, many of our monitors attended events and scenes of incidents and reported on them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can I ask the Registry, perhaps, to bring up document 1D-121, and it's at ERN 1D00-1596 to 1598.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, sir, that is under tab 13, 1-3, of your binder. Sir, would you agree that this would appear to be an internal OSCE e-mail, dated 10th of July, 2001?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it is being sent from the OSCE Spillover Monitor Mission to Skopje; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it is addressed to Ambassador Stoudmann. Can you recall who he was at the time.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: No, I am sorry. I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, if we go down this page, sir, there is a paragraph which starts in those words: "I'm working on a supplemental report that will address recent developments. The allegations with regard to alleged the human rights violation by EAAG have increased and now include..." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And they include, under number one,"Illegal detentions of civilians." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "Forced labour," under number 2?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "Forced conscription," under number 3?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Under number four, "The use of juveniles in military operation or within an area of engagement." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Under number five, "Physical abuse and intimidation of assistants at NLA check-points."

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Under number six, it refers to "Ethnic cleansing."

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Under number 7, "Looting."

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Number 8, "Wanton destruction of property."

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Under number 9, it refers to the use of mine and goes on to say that the "EAAG is the only warring party known to have used mines." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Is that correct to what as to what it says or what the situation was?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And under number 10, it refers to "Initiating hostilities in area known to be inhabited by civilian, including children." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say this: "A videotape of the armed activities in Tetovo, immediately prior to the cease-fire, shows children playing in a field immediately adjacent to an area, from which the EAAG initiated automatic weapons fire, and running away in terror as the shooting continues." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And under 11, sir, it also refers to murder of an unarmed civilian; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this document at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D16, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, I assume you have deliberately omitted tendering certain documents that you put to the witness and got answers on; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, partly, Your Honour. I think one of them I have simply forgotten and will do that now, and that will be the document under tab 11. That is 1D-119, 1D00-1587, and that is the Paris Declaration of the OSCE. As for the report of the 16th of August, Your Honour, I will come back to it with this witness, and I will seek to tender it once I have asked questions from Mr. Bolton.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Paris Declaration will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D17, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: May I ask the Registry to bring up document 1D-122, and that is ERN 1D00-1599.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, that is document 14, 1-4. Would you agree, sir, that this is a special report prepared by your organisation concerning human rights related complaints related to the EAAG in the Tetovo area?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: It appears to be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if I may draw your attention to the first paragraph of that document, where it say this: "The allegations under investigation are related not only to the groups treatment of ethnic Macedonians in the Tetovo area, but also towards persons in the ethnic Albanian community who objected to the EAAG's activity." I'm afraid I can't read the last three words. But would you agree that that is what this document says?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You will recall, I hope, that you have been asked by my colleague about villages that were under the control of the NLA. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I ask you to turn your attention to the second paragraph of that document then. It says this: "The mission specialists confirmed reports from the OSCE's Tetovo area monitors that, even during the cease-fire, the ethnic Macedonian civilian population north of Tetovo is under heavy pressure from EAAG to leave." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It goes on to say this: "These pressures take the form of kidnappings, temporary detentions, and serious, persistent forms of intimidation and restrictions on the movement of civilians attempting to engage in ordinary activities such as agriculture, shopping, and going to work." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it goes to say this: "The conduct of the EAAG is consistent with an attempt to ethnically cleanse that area." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You have also been asked by Mr. Saxon about what, I think, was called authority bodies and check-points set up by the NLA. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If i may ask you to move on, then, to the third paragraph of that document, which starts with the word, "furthermore." And in the middle of this paragraph, it says this: "The EAAG is currently engaging in action associated the with civilian admission of the area under their control; for instance, regulating traffic, conducting 'police patrols,' closing brothels." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It goes on to say this: "Unfortunately, their treatment of ethnic Macedonian civilians in the course of this activities actively discourages a perception that said community would be safe, let alone fairly treated, should the EAAG remain in control of their current area of influence in this region." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it concludes thus: "To the extent the EAAG is engaged in behaviour that creates intolerable conditions for ethnic Macedonians during the cease-fire, it is both destabilising the cease-fire and discouraging the political settlement." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then I will ask to you move on to the next page, the first paragraph, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: For the Registry, that would be 1D00-1600.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You were asked also, I believe, about check-points that were set up by the NLA. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that's what the OSCE reports says about check-points in Tetovo: "The mission has received numerous allegations of kidnappings beatings, robberies, and intimidation of ethnic Macedonians at EAAG check-points." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And IT goes to say that: "Check-points are themselves a violation of the cease-fire agreement." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then, sir, you were also asked about the proportion of ethnic Albanians in the police forces. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And I think you gave an estimate of one to 80; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is that to say that it is a general estimate on your part and that you didn't see figures in that regard?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, if I may draw your attention, perhaps, to the third paragraph of that document, which starts with the words, "The mission is most likely..." Can you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would like to read the sentence in the middle of there, says as follows: "As of 23rd of July, the mission has received credible allegations that 25 persons have disappeared are allegedly detained by the EAAG operating in Tetovo area." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It goes on to say: "This number includes ethnic Macedonian civilians and ethnic Albanians who were serving in the Ministry of Interior as regular officers or as reservists at the time of their disappearance." Can you read that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And would you agree, sir, that such kidnapping could very well be a [indiscernible] disincentive to joining the Ministry?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And I will then ask you to go on to the last paragraph on that page, which starts with the words "Human rights," and it say this: "Human rights related complaints specific to the alleged conduct of the EAAG in the Tetovo area now include: Illegal detention of civilians; beatings and other physical abuse; forced labour; detained person report having been forced to dig ditches; some ethnic Albanians report they were similarly forced to assist the EAAG; forced conscription; use of juveniles in areas of engagement; intimidation of ethnic Macedonian civilians, including women, children, and elderly at check-points; looting and wanton destruction of property; robbery." And if you turn the page over, it will say: "Ethnic cleansing."

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I have a page missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It should be under the number 1D00-1602.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: An extra page, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it goes on to say this: "And engaging in a fire-fight with automatic weapons without warning in an area immediately adjacent to civilian dwellings and where children were at play." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D18, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, are you also aware of the fact that the NLA would sometimes intentionally target religion and historic sites?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And would you be familiar with the incident of the Leshok Monastery?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And could you tell this Chamber what happened with this monastery or can you simply confirm that the monastery was destroyed by the NLA?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I can confirm that there was extensive. I did not myself visit that location. It was outside my area of responsibility, but I was well aware of reporting coming from the monitors who were responsible for that area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And are you also aware, sir, that the fact that the NLA would use religious or historical sites or buildings as military emplacement?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Including mosques; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I, perhaps, show you a document which is dated -- which covers the period 1 to the 15 of August, and that is under tab 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would be 1D-123 under the ERN number -- well, the Registry has it already.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, if I may ask you to turn to the last page of that document, that would be 1606, and focus your attention on the second paragraph or first full paragraph, and it says this: "Two further observations are also important. There has been a clear tendency on the part of the Tetovo NLA to use religious and historic site as military installation or bases of operations." Can you read that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And does that conform with your own experience?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it goes on to say this: "Military emplacements are also located in positions where they are on fire, includes religious and historic sites. There is particular concern for the painted mosque and the Teks [phoen] Monastery. The misuse of religious sites as military installation must be condemned. It should be noted in the case of the Teks, it appears the NLA was attempting to force the Macedonian forces to fire on the site for propaganda purposes." Can you read that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you confirm that this report is, again, an OSCE report covering the period of 1 to 15 August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: It certainly appears to be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would you agree sir that one particular problem relating to your monitoring, as you call it, or investigation of human rights violation related to the fact that the NLA would sometime pressure or intimidate the population with whom you had to deal with?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes. We were not tasked to investigate. We were tasked to report what had occurred. But, yes, in essence, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if I may draw your attention, again, on the same document, sir, that is just under last paragraph but one, starting in those words: "Finally, it should be noted that investigation of human rights related incidents is complicated by the problem that the NLA is applying pressure to its own people, and must be considered as a possible source of human rights abuses to ethnic Albanians, including beatings and murders." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it goes on say that: "Whilst the NLA officially denies engaging in human rights abuses of ethnic Macedonians, such actions are privately acknowledged in conversations with many person who speak own their behalf. Ethnic Albanian of some professional standing and stature have in the same breath denied that the NLA has engaged in human rights violation, while vigorously acknowledging that, of course, the NLA has executed, beaten, and threatened 'collaborators' and also destroyed their property." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will also seek to tender this document at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D19, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, you will recall that during your visits on the -- well, let's bring that back perhaps. Going back to the 10th of August, were you aware at the time that the NLA had a presence in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: At that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And were you aware of any information having been received by your organisation to that effect at that time?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, may I ask the Registry to bring up document 1D-124, under the ERN 1D00-1607.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it is the under tab 16, sir, of your binder. As you will see from the cover, it says that it is a daily bulletin of non-compliance with the cease-fire from 1800 hours on 9 August, 2001 to 1800 hours on 10 August 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if I ask you to simply focus on the bottom right-hand corner, you will see that this document comes from the mission archives of the OSCE; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if I may ask you to turn your attention to page 1618, that will be page number 12 of this document, and ask to you focus on the number 37 item on this list. And it relates from the earliest record to the 10th of August, and it says this: "At 1530, a patrol from the police station Mirkovci reported that in the house of the family Zendelovski in the village Ljuboten, three persons were dressed in black uniforms and armed with auto weapons." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I can see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was that information which you had in your possession at the time?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But have you no reason to believe that it was not in the possession of the OSCE at the time, in view of the fact that --

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I will also tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D20, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to move on to the 11th of August, if I may. And you will recall that on that day, again, you heard mortar and infantry fire coming from above the hills above Ljuboten. And I think you have indicated that you heard this -- the sound of mortar and infantry weapons at around 7.30 in the morning, early in the morning; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I seem to recall that it was early in the morning, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the sound of fire was clearly audible from Radisani; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Very much so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you able, at the time, to locate the origin of the fire?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Approximately. We were able to observe impact, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the impact that you witnessed were on the ridge above the village of Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Above Ljubanci, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Hmm. And is that correct that you -- the first impression that you form was that one side was trying, and I think you used the expression "to clear the other." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I may have used that expression. I believe there was a clearance operation in place, clearing the area. I can relate that in military terms, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But you have indicated, also, that later on you heard heavy gun-fire coming from the same general area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is that also correct, sir, that you formed the view then that the activity and fighting in the hills was between the NLA and security forces of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That was my belief, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, that was a belief that was shared by your colleague, Mr. Rogic?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On that day, sir -- I mean, I don't want to go through all your evidence because the statement has been admitted. But on that day, you left your headquarters in Radisani and, again, went towards the village of Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you able to reach the village on that day?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I don't recall. No, we weren't. I don't believe we were. I don't recall accurately, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand that you indicated that on that day you saw a great crowd of angry civilians on the road from Radisani to Ljuboten. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you also recall having been advised by the police not to go to Ljuboten for your own security; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You have indicated to the Prosecutor that you had an agreement with, I think, between the OSCE and the government about your freedom to travel around the country; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And on that day, sir, you were eventually allowed to go through and towards the village of Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sitting here trying to recall exactly which day we went in there. We attempted many times, and we did at some point get into the village, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, you didn't see any police check-points on your way from Radisani up to Ljuboten up to Ljuboten, that is?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yeah. There's -- there was police check-point which was permanently there. It had a name and I can't remember what it was now, but there was a semi-permanent police check-point on the route.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In the proximity of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: On the road to Ljuboten, yes. On a ridge that we regularly travelled along, whenever we did go to the village, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But you were not stopped on that day at that check-point?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: We would have been stopped, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You were allowed through?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes. We didn't bypass the police check-points in that way, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's move on to the 12th of August, if I may. You've indicated in your statement or on your notes, rather, that early in the morning, between 8.00 and 8.05, you heard what you believe to be a loud mortar round; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And shortly thereafter, you saw a large plumb of smoke coming from a location from within the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It was close to the Orthodox church?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the Registry please bring up, I think it is photo number 4. It is a panorama picture of the village of Ljuboten. It has the ERN N005-7065.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to see on that picture the place where you saw that smoke coming from? If you want the picture to be focussed on one particular part of this panorama, we can certainly arrange for that.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yeah. Can we enlarge the right-hand side, yeah, and go left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you able to see the location where you saw that smoke coming from on that day?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Not precisely. It would help if there was a southern view of it, which was the view that I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you see the general area, perhaps, where the smoke could have been coming from? Can you identify that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, with the assistance of the usher, could you mark this general location.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: As I say, it is difficult to be precise from this view, but I believe it was approximately this area. It may have been -- may have been have been this area, but in that rough direction or that rough location.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We'll tender that picture, Your Honour, at this stage. We'll attempt with also a southern version of this photograph. At this stage, we will tender this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I wonder, Mr. Bolton, whether you could mark a number 1 in the lower of the two areas you have circled.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Because that seemed from your evidence to be your preferred memory of the location, and the second and alternative possibility. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is very difficult. I wouldn't, at this stage, wish to preference either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, there's no need to mark the second, as long as we know 1 is the one you first marked.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D21 Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, I will try to show you a picture form the southern perspective to see whether it facilitate the identification of location.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that will be N005-7603.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, sir, please feel free to direct the Registry to the area which --

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: If we could zoom in on the left-hand side, please. A little further. Can we go further?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you able to locate the position from --

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yeah, I believe so. It was the -- in the area of this white wall here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We'll tender this as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D22, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And after this first loud explosion, sir, is it correct that you heard two similar explosions shortly thereafter?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you also understood that that they landed in the general area where you had seen the first round land; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: They were closer together, to each other, but separate, slightly separate from the first impact or first detonation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you understood or you heard, rather, a number of mortars being fired in response to this origin of fire. Is that what you understood?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Following those original three detonations, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is that correct that you understood the first three detonation to have been come the NLA, sir?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That was my belief.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And your belief was that those three mortars from the NLA were directed at the police post, next to the church; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: There were potential targets in that area for the NLA, one of which was a police location.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you understood the later fire, that is, after the first three rounds, to have been the response of the army to this original fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I didn't know what they were in response to, but they followed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you understood those to come from the army position.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to show you --

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: The security forces position, I wasn't in a position to say whether it was army, police. I can't say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you assist me, if I could intrude, Mr. Mettraux. The responsive fire, were you able to see the fall of that fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At times, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And where was that? Is it in the village or out of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was further to the right of this photograph, pretty much on the right-hand edge of this photograph, as it is shown now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Within the village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Within the village, yes, Your Honour. At times, we could see the smoke of what we believed to be impact detonations, and these were impact detonations that we believe came from mortar bombs that were fired into that location. At times, that smoke was not -- we couldn't see the impact, the explosion, but we could see the smoke rising from those explosions or those detonations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In one or two of his questions, Mr. Mettraux has used the phrase "responsive fire. " I saw in that the possibility that the responding fire was aimed at the source of the original firing. Is that what you were meaning, or were you describing something differently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I can refer to my military background, the -- it was unlikely, in n my view, that the firing position of the first three detonations was within the village, because it is very close, for what I believe to be a heavy mortar. In that respect, the detonations, that we saw that corresponded with the security forces position firing, were not landing in the area -- in an area that I would expect to find a firing position, if that clarifies the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. And was the responsive fire apparently a similar calibre mortar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was a smaller one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And in number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To be specific, the first three detonations both I and my colleague believed were probably 120-millimetre mortars. Subsequent explosions were medium mortars, 81-, 82-millimetre mortars, and we estimated somewhere in the region of 60 rounds fired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sorry, Mr. Mettraux, but there was an area there that I thought we might as well explore and finish with.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I may perhaps assist further, Your Honour. I will ask the Registry to bring up document 1D-125, and it is under the ERN 1D00-1634.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, it is under tab 18 of your binder. I think that will be the next one on your binder, and, again, that would be an OSCE spot report of the 14th of August, 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I may ask you to focus on point --

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, I have 13th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, the document we have is dated 14th of August. I think this is the this one, yes. Sorry, my mistake. Yeah. If I may ask you to focus on the letter B, on the first page, under the heading "Central Area." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It says that: "Ljuboten remains a focal point of interest, with accusation in the media that there have been extrajudicial killings of three people in the village, in addition to a further three women and four men killed during the firing on Sunday." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I may ask to focus on the last paragraph but one, it says this: "It now seems clear that the EAAG mortar fire brought to bear onto the ethnic Macedonian part of the village originally sparked the fighting, and at least a covert presence of EAAG did in fact exist in the village." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I can see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we're going to tender this at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D23, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful. And I will ask the Registry to bring back the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That is under tab 2 of your binder, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That is under the ERN 1D00-1532, I would believe. That would be incorrect, actually. It is N001-5356, and that would be the third page of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, if I may ask you to focus on the fourth paragraph on that page, with the paragraph started "On 12th of August." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It says this: "On 12 of August, at 8.05 hours, the first mortar round fell on the village. It landed in the vicinity of the Orthodox church in the Macedonian section of the village." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is that consistent with your observations?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "Two more rounds followed, each closer to the church. All three are believed to have been 120-millimetre mortars." Again, is it consistent with your observations?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "These are more likely to have been EAAG rounds than government, and were the first shots fired into the village. Thereafter, the army fired on the Albanian side of the village with its smaller calibre mortars." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That's a what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is that consistent with your observations?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The next question that I have -- or the next point that I would like to bring up with you is in the same document, sir, a bit further down. That's the last paragraph but one, and that is the conclusion of the author of that report about the exchange of fire. And it starts with the word "In any event." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It says this: "It is clear that Macedonian fire on the village was directed at the north edge of town, particularly near the fields, and it appears that the security forces moved up through this area in an action to clear it of any hostile forces that might be located there." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "It is also within the realm of possibility that the death of the first two men occurred during that operation." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will tender it at this stage, although I will use it again in the course of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, a fair reading of this document shows that a number of portions are highly inconsistent, if I may say, with the earlier report that was tendered during examination-in-chief that had been authored by this witness. And so the Prosecution is concerned that really the probative value and reliability of this document has not been established. And to establish it, I think some additional questions need to be asked of this witness regarding other portions of this document and the person who authored it and how it was created. Now, Mr. Mettraux could do that during cross-examination, or if the Court prefers, the document could be marked for identification now and the Prosecution could pursue this on redirect before any final decision is made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it not an OSCE report?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And we have been to date receiving OSCE reports, including a number not directly authored by the witness. From my point of view, the appropriate approach would be to receive the document because of its apparent credibility due to its source, to leave it then for re-examination, to explore further the reliability of its content, a matter to be taken into account by the Chamber in its eventual weighing of it. You followed all that, Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. There might be a few issues with which Mr. Bolton may want to take issue with the content of that document. At this stage, he hasn't taken issue it; and as you pointed out, if the Prosecution think there a discrepancies between the two, it can deal with that in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, in our experience, there are likely to be some various ranges of qualities in a document like this. And individual officers of an organisation like OSCE might well embrace parts of a report, not necessarily others. But the overall document has a credibility due to the nature of its source; and if there are particular issues, I think they can be adequately explored in the process of your cross-examination, perhaps Mr. Apostolski's, and Mr. Saxon's re-examination. So this document will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D24, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, there is another document I would like to ask you to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That is document 1D-127, under the ERN 1D00-1640.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's under your tab 20 in the binder. As you can see, sir, this is a report related to the military activities on 12th of August, 2001. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it is records the fact that: "On the 12th of August, 2001, in the morning, I was at the rest house performing my regular duties; and about 8.00, we heard main long lasting repeated shots." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you can see from the signature, the "I" stands for Captain Grozdanovski [phoen], a commander of a mortar battery. If you continue through that document, you will see that: "Later, the commander of the battalion called me and ordered me to visit the observation post at check-point Smoke, and to prepare the battery for action." Can you see that? It's the second sentence of the first paragraph sir.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if I may ask you now to turn to the second paragraph, it says this: "From the observation towards the village, I realised that the terrorists were firing from the area of the church, from an old house about 100 metres under the mosque. Most probably, there was a sniper; whereas, above the mosque, from the new houses, the second one, there was a machine-gun firing towards us." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "Then I informed the commander about the situation, and he ordered me to destroy those positions with several mortar shells from a 120-millimetre mortar." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it goes on to say this: "In the period of time between 9.00 and 10.00 hours, we fired several mortar shells as follows: Around the church, we fired eight mortar shells; towards the sniper, we fired five mortar shells; whereas, towards the machine-gun, we fired three mortar shells; at the military activities in the area of Ljuboten village, we fired altogether 16 120-millimetre mortar shells." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say: "The military activities continued, even afterwards; but because the police had entered the village, I did not engage anymore the battery after 10.00, towards Ljuboten village." May I ask you, sir, whether that is consistent with your own observations?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Can I just have a moment to read through it again?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Certainly. Perhaps to assist you, this identifies three firing positions from the terrorists: One from the area of the church; the second one from an old house, about 100 metre from the new houses; and then one from above the mosque. And then he goes to say that they fired eight mortars at the area towards the church, five towards the second location where the sniper was, and three towards the location where the machine-gun was.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Can you repeat your question to me? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The question was, essentially, whether some aspects - I'm not suggesting that you might have observed all of these events - but does this description of what happened in that part of the village coincide with or at least consistent with your own observations or a part thereof.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: A part thereof. It is my belief that there were more mortar rounds fired in that area, or certainly that impacted in that area, than this would account for.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, we will come to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the Registry -- well, first, I will tender this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D25, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will ask --

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Can I add that I'm referring only to the mortar fire, and I did not observe any small arms fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if the Registry can now bring up document 1D-128, under the ERN 1D00-1642.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's, sir, another similar military report of the same day. This one is signed by Lieutenant Braznjarkovski [phoen] Darko, and this report suggests that at around 8.00 in the morning, an army position above Ljuboten, again, "smoke was targeted by machine-gun and sniper fire." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Mm-hm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, it goes on to say that an order was given to respond to enemy fire and to shell the position from which fire was coming from inside the village. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the report identifies three positions from which the fire was coming from the village, and I will list them for you and you will tell me whether that's the correct ones. It says that: "The machine-gun position was located left from the mosque; a sniper position from the house under the mosque."

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry. Can you -- oh, yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "And, finally, a mortar position in the direction of the village graveyard." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That's what it says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say that the army returned fire to all three positions, with six mortars towards the first position, five towards the second, and five in the general direction of the graveyard. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That's what it says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, sir, would that be generally consistent with your observations or a part thereof?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: A part thereof. That would account for some more of the mortar bombs that I believe landed in that area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will seek to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As Exhibit 1D26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we will have to interrupt you, Mr. Mettraux. I'm sorry. We will have the second break now, and resume at five minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bolton, I attempted to make a modest contribution to the completion strategy of the Tribunal by speaking fast, and I have been reminded by many interpreters that I should slow down and should pass on the message to you. So if we can both try not no overlap with each other and perhaps take a bit more time, I shall endeavor to do that. Your Honour, I would also like to bring to your attention another matter which the Registry tree kindly pointed out to us, and this relates to one exhibit which we have tendered. We referred to it as Rule 65 ter 223, but in fact what we have tendered and what has been admitted are the first five pages of that document, which consist of the report which I have been discussing with Mr. Bolton. And for the record, the ERN range of that document is N001-5356 to N001-53601. I'm grateful to the Registry for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sir, we left off at 12th of August, and I would just like to ask you a two or three more questions about that day. The first one is: You would confirm that you did not enter the village on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do I understand properly that the reason why you did not or could not enter the village on that day was because of the animosity of the civilians, or some civilians in any case, that were around the village and the animosity which they showed to your team; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: There was -- when we tried to approach the village initially, right at the beginning following the mine strike, there was animosity from the villagers in Ljubanci. Subsequently, we did not meet with animosity when trying to approach Ljuboten from the other direction, which was further to the east avoiding Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And was there any particular reason why you did not attempt to enter the village on that day? Was it the same animosity?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: There was no animosity, but there was --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The potential?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: -- a determination on, on one occasion, not to let us past, and there was also occasions when we were stopped by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you ask to it go through or was it your own determination that the risk was too great to get into the village on that day?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: We had no intention to drive into the middle of an exchange of fire. But nonetheless we were, on occasion, stopped by civilians and did not want to provoke an incident and on other occasions stopped by police, and, again, did not want to provoke an incident by pushing the matter further, by driving through, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is that when the police officer explained to you that they were doing that for the purpose of your own security; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: There is another matter, sir, I would like to bring back these notes taken by Mr. Tucker which have been marked as 1D12, and that would be the third and last page of that document. It's the first tab of your binder, sir. That would be the previous document, I believe. If you --

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. If you focus on the third paragraph on that page, it records the following event, incident of fact in any case. It says, "he," that's you, Mr. Bolton, "and Vladimir Rogac were trying to facilitate this movement," that's the movement of the villagers," and were in contact the HQ who in turn were in contact with the Crisis Management Committee. The ICRC were also involved ..." Can you remember trying to facilitate the evacuations of the villagers on that day?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you also recall that the Crisis Management Centre was notified of that fact and that a request for police assistance was made?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I am not privy to the conversations that took place between the -- our headquarters and the Crisis Management Centre. However, we reported everything back to them, and all our requests were at that point channelled through them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And are you aware that shortly thereafter the Crisis Management Centre in fact sent a police unit or police group to assist with the evacuation, or is that a fact that you are not aware of?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to move on now to the 14th, sir, the 14th of August, when you entered the village at last. I won't go through your evidence again, but I think you explained in your statement that you considered that the best course of action was for you to contact the police to ask an investigative judge to attend; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you recall,, sir, whom in the police you called at the time to ask for the investigative judge to come?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: We had a -- I believe, a number of conversations with the police both directly and indirectly. I refer there to other organisations that were involved in this also. There was ICRC and there was UNHCR. And we were speaking both directly and indirectly there to the command element of Skopje police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you remember the name of that person? Was it Mr. Bliznakovski?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: And -- there were two people, I think, that were on the Macedonian police side involved in that conversation. Those communications which Mr. Petro Stojnovski [phoen] and Mr. Bliznakovski, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And would you agree that there those were the people who had negotiated your safe passage to the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I specifically don't recall that particular incident, of them facilitating our movement at that time. But certainly on other occasions they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And on that occasion, sir, the police allowed you through without any problem to the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And they also --

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: There was brief delay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. And they also arranged for an investigative judge to come to the Cair police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Now that I don't know. I don't know where that -- I don't know of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'll come back to that. Now you explained, I think, in your statement that you had a number of conversations with the police in Cair thereafter. Is that correct? Through the police, to the investigative judge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: I was not in Cair -- Cair myself, if you're referring to the police station there. And I do not know the location of the police that we were talking, because it was via telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Is that correct, sir, that, I mean, you were able to enter the village without any difficulty and there was no interference on the part of the police during your stay in the village?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you were left to do what you wanted at that time?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you now a few questions about your observations in the village and in particular your observations of the bodies of the five deceased. Is that correct, sir - and that may be an obvious question - that you had no ballistic or forensic information at the time?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: Regarding what?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Regarding the circumstances or causes of death of these five individuals.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: No, that's correct. I had no forensic information relating to those five bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And am I correct to understand then that the conclusions that you drew were based solely on your discussions with some of the villagers and your own observations?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: And my own experience --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And your own experience.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON
utterances.text: -- and knowledge of fire-arms and the effect of -- of bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And would you say, or am I correct in stating your position as follows. That the -- your observations about the two -- the first two men that you observed were particularly suspicious, if I can put that in those terms?
